Theme

Town, shops & places · Money, work & business

sell verb

also selling, be sold, is sold, sold for, for sale (be sold), at what price do these go for?, how much did you sell it for?

classical

Traupman 131

vēndō, vēndere, vēndidī, vēnditum

verb, third conjugation

From vēnum dō.

Other words

  • vēneō, vēnīre, vēniī — be sold

    verb, irregular, conjugated like eō: the passive of vēndō, conjugation · classical · Vulg. Mt. 10.29: duo passerēs asse vēneunt; Plaut. Men. 1158: vēnībunt servī; Traupman 130; Traupman 322

    “Be sold” is not a passive of vēndō, which classical prose does not use apart from the participles vēnditus, vēndendus (Lewis & Short), but vēneō, “go to sale”: vēneunt, they are sold; vēnībunt, they will be sold; vēnīsse, to have been sold.

  • vēnditāre — keep offering for sale

    also used · classical · Traupman 131

Examples

  • Quantī hoc vēndis?

    How much are you selling this for?composed

  • Nōnne duo passerēs asse vēneunt?

    Aren’t two sparrows sold for a penny?Vulg. Mt. 10.29

  • vēnībunt servī, supellex, fundī, aedēs, omnia. vēnībunt quīquī licēbunt, praesentī pecūniā.

    For sale: slaves, furniture, farms, house, everything. They will be sold for whatever they fetch, cash down.Plaut. Men. 1158–1159

  • eum forte agrum in quō ipse castra habēret vēnīsse nihil ob id dēminūtō pretiō

    that the very field he was camped on had been sold, at no lower price for thatLiv. 26.11.6

  • surgite: jam vēndit puerīs jentācula pistor

    get up: the baker is already selling the boys their breakfastMart. 14.223.1

  • Quibus pretiīs hae mercēs vēneunt?

    At what price do these items go for?Traupman 131

  • Quantī hoc vēnit?

    How much did this sell for?Traupman 131

See also seller, buy, for sale, sold out, price.
